findGuestTable.name: Find the Guest's Table
findGuestTable.description: Write a function that takes the array of guests' full names, the matching array of table names, and an arriving guest announced as an honorific and a surname. Return the name of the table that guest is sitting at, or `"No table found"` if they aren't on the seating plan.

solveTightly.name: Solve it in 9 lines
solveTightly.description: Bonus: this can be written far more compactly than you might expect. Try and solve this in 9 lines of code or fewer.

emptyList.name: Empty seating plan
emptyList.description: Nobody's sitting anywhere when the plan is empty.

nameMissing.name: Brad's turned away
nameMissing.description: The name's not on the seating plan.

namePresent.name: Brad's shown to his seat
namePresent.description: Brad Pitt is on the plan, so Mr Pitt gets his table.

differentHonorific.name: Knight of the realm
differentHonorific.description: A different honorific, and a guest who isn't first on the plan.

bondSeated.description: James Bond is on the plan.

bondNotSeated.description: Only Jason Bourne is on the plan, not James Bond.

partialSurname.description: Neither Ada Spitt nor Hugo Ross-Pitt is Mr Pitt, so he has no seat here.

lloydWebber.name: How about a Baron?
lloydWebber.description: Baron Lloyd Webber has two words in his surname.

markWebber.name: Is Mark the Baron?
markWebber.description: A different Webber doesn't count - the surname has to match in full.

formalDinnerBonusLineCount.name: Neat and tidy: Lord Doyle
formalDinnerBonusLineCount.description: The same seating plan as before, but this time try and solve this in 9 lines of code or fewer.

twoLists.question: How do the two arrays relate to each other?
twoLists.answer: They're a pair. The first guest sits at the first table, the second guest at the second table, and so on. So it's not enough to know *that* a guest is on the plan - you need to know *where* on the plan they are.

comparingNames.question: The guest says 'Mr Pitt' but the plan says 'Brad Pitt'. How do I compare those?
comparingNames.answer: Those two strings will never be equal, so a straight comparison won't get you anywhere. Have a think about which part of what the guest announced actually appears on the plan, and whereabouts in the plan's entry you'd expect to find it.

lookalikeSurnames.question: Could a surname match the wrong guest?
lookalikeSurnames.answer: It absolutely could. Read 'Ada Spitt' and 'Hugo Ross-Pitt' out loud, and then think about Mr Pitt. Ask yourself what makes a surname a real surname on that line, rather than just some letters that happen to sit at the end of it.

noMatch.question: What should I return when nobody matches?
noMatch.answer: The string `"No table found"`, exactly as written. The trickier bit is knowing when you're allowed to say it. If you've checked the very first guest on the plan and they're not your man, do you actually know yet that he isn't seated somewhere?
